newsitem.title: CHINA: China says Asia should look after own security.
newsitem.headline: China says Asia should look after own security.

text.p: China said on Tuesday it opposed the stationing in Asia of troops from outside the region, saying Asian nations should look after themselves.
"We believe Asian nations should preserve the peace and stability of the Asian region," Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang told a regular news briefing.

"We believe Asian nations are fully capable of doing so," he said in reply to a question about U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen's remarks that U.S. troops should stay in South Korea even if peace comes to the divided Korean peninsula.
Cohen made the remarks at the weekend. On Tuesday, he said in Tokyo that any reduction in U.S. troops in the Western Pacfic could trigger a dangerous arms race in Asia.
Cohen also said the 100,000 U.S. troops in the region, mostly in Japan and South Korea, were not aimed at containing China, and that even a partial withdrawal could frighten U.S. allies.
The Chinese spokesman said Beijing's position has always been to oppose the stationing of foreign troops in the region.
